title: Grigio or Gris
subtitle: Two names, two styles
objectives: Explain what Pinot Grigio usually means
Explain what Pinot Gris usually means

steps.title: Pinot Grigio
steps.body: Pinot Grigio, in the Italian style, is light-bodied, crisp and neutral, with lemon, green apple and almond. It's usually picked early, fermented cool in steel and bottled young. Its simplicity and freshness made it one of the best-selling white wines in the UK and US. Producers elsewhere use the name to signal this style.

steps.title: Pinot Gris
steps.body: Pinot Gris, in the Alsace style, is fuller and richer, with ripe pear, honey, ginger, smoke and spice, sometimes off-dry. It's picked riper, often from low-yield sites. Alsace's dry, sunny autumns and Grand Cru vineyards give some of the most concentrated versions. Oregon and New Zealand often use the name for richer styles.

steps.prompt: A New Zealand label says Pinot Gris rather than Pinot Grigio. What does it most likely signal?
steps.explanation: Producers use Gris to signal the fuller Alsace style.

steps.body: When choosing, read the name as a style guide: Grigio for a light aperitif, Gris for a fuller wine with food.

steps.prompt: Alsace Pinot Gris can be off-dry.
steps.explanation: Yes. Ripe Alsace Pinot Gris sometimes has some residual sugar.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Pinot Grigio means light, crisp and neutral
Pinot Gris means rich, spicy and riper
Alsace makes the most concentrated Pinot Gris
